description: Every brief so far used hand-CUDA (load_inline); NONE used Triton, despite the operator's explicit 'primarily use Triton' directive and the two leaders who beat us using it (revolutionaryspaces submission_eigh_n32_parallel, msaroufim triton_diagonal_fast_path). The megakernel that serves shapes 2/3/8/12 (via brief-11 inner-solve routing) does its O(n^3) tridiagonalization trailing-updates + compact-WY back-transform in SIMT (brief-3 found hand-WMMA 'cast-bound'); ncu shows it barrier-bound at 50% occupancy, zero tensor-core usage. Build a TRITON batched medium-n symmetric eigensolver (n in ~256-512) whose O(n^3) parts run on tensor cores via tl.dot with Triton autotuning (block sizes, num_warps, num_stages) -- the tiling/FP16-cast management Triton does automatically where hand-WMMA was cast-bound. Structure: batched two-sided reduction (panel Householder, trailing update = tl.dot FP16/TF32 across the batch), the banked Sturm-bisection eigenvalues, back-transform via tl.dot through the WY reflectors, FP32 Rayleigh for L. Route the shapes where it beats the current megakernel/cuSOLVER through the existing router with per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback. Exploit the loose gate (eigen<=1.2%, orth<=0.6%) for low-precision tl.dot. Forks best 12251fe. -O2-equivalent determinism (Triton is deterministic by default); no 'stream' substring; do not regress shapes 1/2/3/8/12.

Triton tcgen05 batched eigensolver (_tc_eigh) wired as the low-rank inner solve for k in (32,448], replacing SIMT mega_eigh_med_k (48.9% of n=512 shape-3). Panel Householder tridiag with O(n^3) trailing-update + back-transform via tl.dot FP16 (tcgen05 HMMA confirmed in PTX); banked Sturm bisection + twisted eigvecs; FP32 Rayleigh L. Validates PASS all 39 test shapes. Benchmark 58109us (REGRESSION vs parent 41378): the per-column A@v inside the panel is ~350 separate tiny tl.dot GEMV launches -> latency-bound, negates TC. shape3 n=512b640 387512us. Fix: batch the panel A@V into one GEMM.

symv off tensor cores (torch.bmm for the batched N=1 A@v), tl.dot only for the true GEMMs (trailing update/back-transform/Q-accum), panel 32->64. Benchmark 56424us (t1 58109, parent 41378) -- still a large regression. shape3 n=512b640 348326us. The panel reduction issues ~n sequential torch.bmm GEMV launches (memory-bound); the SIMT megakernel fuses the whole reduction in SMEM (one launch, no HBM round-trips) and beats GEMM-per-step. Tensor cores accelerate only trailing-update+backtransform, not the symv that dominates tridiagonalization. Next: two-stage dense->band->tridiag so the band reduction is all-GEMM, or serve the n=512 shapes cuSOLVER handles today (mixed512/lapack_dense512) with a direct full-n TC solve.

Fused panel-factorization Triton kernel (_tc_panel_kernel, latrd: whole panel's reflectors+W-vectors+taus in one launch, n/panel launches instead of ~n). Fixed 'stream' banned substring in comments. Validates PASS all 39 shapes. Benchmark 53522us (t2 56424, parent 41378) -- still regressed. shape3 n=512b640 361307us. The in-kernel symv p=A@v reads the full nxn A from GLOBAL per column (serial, one CTA/matrix, low occupancy); the megakernel does the same symv from SMEM (~19TB/s) which is why it wins. Reduction is memory-bound on the symv; the tl.dot trailing update is cheap but can't offset a slow global-memory symv. Direction: either hold the trailing panel in SMEM (like megakernel) or abandon Householder for a GEMM-only reduction (SBR dense->band with the panel symv replaced by a block GEMM).

Direct tensor-core full-n solve for n=512 (diagnostic). Restored megakernel inner solve (_TC_INNER=False), added residual-gated _eigh_tc_safe with cuSOLVER fallback, routed all n=512 through it. Validates PASS. Benchmark 76888us (REGRESSION): every n=512 shape slower -- mixed512 605258us and lapack_dense_even512 575356us (both cuSOLVER-bound in parent) are ~4x cuSOLVER's syevd loop. Decisive finding: _tc_eigh full-n LOSES to cuSOLVER because the Householder symv reduction is memory-bound (in-kernel global matvec, one CTA/matrix) and cuSOLVER's fused syevd is far better; the tl.dot trailing-update+back-transform are ~1% of time. Tensor cores can only dominate the reduction via SBR (dense->band with block-QR so the panel symv becomes a block GEMM). Open: build SBR stage-1 on tensor cores.

Full SBR eigensolver: _sbr_dense_to_band (correct dense->band block-QR, ALL O(n^3) work = tl.dot GEMMs; two-sided WY update derived+verified: recon 0.0096, eigval 0.0026, off-band exactly 0) + fused Householder band->tridiag, routed n=512 via _eigh_tc_safe. Reduced tl.dot autotune to 5 configs. Validation PASSES (test n=512 batch 16). Benchmark FAILS (eval.py 112): lapack_dense_even512 seed780001 batch640 matrix 321 reconstruction residual 0.401 > 0.275 allowed. Root cause: _eigh_tc_safe gate checks eigen+orth but NOT reconstruction -- a bad eigenpair that weakly satisfies A@q~lq and keeps orth slips through. SBR reduction itself is correct+tensor-core; the gate needs a reconstruction term. Will reset and add it.

Added reconstruction-residual gate term to _eigh_tc_safe (eigen+orth+recon in true FP32, thresholds 120/60/250*n*eps below harness 200/100/400); fixes the t5 benchmark failure (matrix 321 now falls to cuSOLVER). Benchmark 98035us PASSES. All n=512 shapes ~1.1-1.2ms: SBR + full-Householder band->tridiag is STRICTLY slower than t4 (76888us) because it ADDS the dense->band reduction on top of a band->tridiag whose Householder symv still walks the full n (O(n^3), doesn't exploit the band). CONFIRMED: SBR stage-1 reduction is correct + all-tensor-core (recon 0.0096, off-band exactly 0), but the win requires an O(n^2 w) bulge-chasing band->tridiag replacing the full Householder. Missing piece = fused SMEM bulge-chase band->tridiag kernel.

Safe non-regressing head: all routing toggles off (_TC_INNER=False, _TC_FULLN=empty, _SBR=False), router parent-equivalent. Benchmark 41429us == parent 41378 within noise (0.12% << 1% floor). Confirms the added Triton kernels (_tc_bmm autotuned tcgen05 GEMM, _tc_panel_kernel fused latrd, _sbr_dense_to_band correct all-TC dense->band, _tc_eigh, _eigh_tc_safe with eigen+orth+recon gate) import with ZERO dormant-code overhead. Branch head carries the full tensor-core + SBR infrastructure (all validated) for a follow-up brief to add the O(n^2 w) bulge-chase band->tridiag that SBR needs to win.

Built the first Triton solver of the run: an autotuned tcgen05 batched GEMM (_tc_bmm, confirmed lowering to tcgen05.mma in PTX on sm_100) + a full batched dense symmetric eigensolver _tc_eigh (panel Householder tridiag, banked Sturm bisection + twisted eigvecs, FP32 Rayleigh L) with the O(n^3) trailing-update + back-transform on tensor cores. Also built a CORRECT all-tensor-core SBR dense->band reduction (_sbr_dense_to_band: recon 0.0096, off-band exactly 0, verified). 7 trials, all validated/gated (per-matrix eigen+orth+RECON residual gate with cuSOLVER fallback). NO IMPROVEMENT over parent 41378us; best safe head = t7 41429us (== parent within 0.12% noise, TC+SBR infra dormant, ZERO import overhead). KEY MEASURED FINDING: tensor cores do NOT help batched medium-n eigh because eigh is dominated by the MEMORY-BOUND Householder symv (A@v matvec, no TC reuse), not the O(n^3) GEMMs -- the tl.dot GEMMs profiled at only ~0.8%, while the SIMT megakernel wins by doing the whole reduction fused in SMEM (one launch, no HBM round-trips). Trials: t1 inner-solve TC 58109us (per-column A@v = ~350 tiny GEMV launches, launch-bound); t2 symv->torch.bmm + panel64 56424us; t3 fused-panel latrd kernel (n/panel launches) 53522us (in-kernel symv reads A from global, serial 1-CTA/matrix); t4 direct full-n TC at n=512 76888us (~4x SLOWER than cuSOLVER's syevd loop on mixed512/lapack_dense512); t5 full SBR FAILED gate (recon slipped, matrix 321); t6 SBR+recon-gate 98035us (SBR adds dense->band ON TOP of a full-Householder band->tridiag that is still O(n^3)). OPEN DIRECTIONS (named, not closed): (1) THE lever -- an O(n^2 w) bulge-chasing band->tridiag (fused SMEM Givens sweep; band of n=512 w=32 = 66KB fits SMEM) to replace the full Householder; SBR stage-1 is already correct+tensor-core so this single missing kernel is what would make SBR beat cuSOLVER/megakernel; (2) a fused SMEM band->tridiag+solve megakernel-style kernel (the band fits SMEM even for n=512/1024, unlike the dense matrix that caps the current megakernel at n<=448) -- could serve n=512/1024 shapes the megakernel cannot; (3) FP8/NVFP4 tl.dot for the trailing-update/back-transform (loose gate admits it) -- untested, would only matter once the reduction stops dominating; (4) the _tc_bmm autotune space was cut to 5 configs for SBR's many shapes -- a per-shape-class tuned set is unswept. The tensor-core GEMM machinery + correct SBR reduction are all on the branch head (dormant) for a follow-up bulge-chase brief to build on.
